sources.citation: Schackow, Diana. 2015. A grammar of Yakkha (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 7). Berlin: Language Science Press. Sect. 2.4.1 pp. 35-36 (Marek variety, Table 2.3) and sect. 3.4 Stress assignment pp. 57-59.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for the Marek/Lumba-Yakkha variety: p. 36 gives 16 comparative words from one Marek speaker and states 'no detailed study has been undertaken yet'; the variety is said to differ so much that 'it cannot be called a dialect of Yakkha any more'. For Yakkha proper (Tumok), sect. 3.4 p. 57: 'by default, the first syllable carries main stress. Closed syllables, however, attract stress. If there are closed syllables, the main stress moves to the last closed syllable, as long as it is not the final syllable of a word'; prefixes are outside the stress domain.

Retirement comment: the Ethnologue entry 'derives from a misinterpretation of the questionnaires used in the Linguistic Survey of Nepal 1981-1984 and should simply be filed under Yakkha (van Driem 2001: 682-683, Schackow 2015: 1-2)'; AES comment 'Yakkha, Chhathare (luu-luu) = 6b (Threatened)'. Zero descriptive references for lumb1250.
